name: AlgoLaser DIY Kit MK3 20W
tagline: Cutting-focused 20W module of the MK3 with a free air pump: 12 mm wood in one pass claimed
tldr: The DIY Kit MK3 20W is the top tier: the MK3's 400 × 400 mm frame, AlgoOS touchscreen and focus stick with a larger 20W diode module and an air pump included. AlgoLaser rates it for 12 mm wood in one pass, the only cutting figure it publishes for the MK3. At $459 it costs $150 more than the 15W. No independent review exists yet to confirm the claim.
mainObjective: Regular wood cutting and faster engraving on a budget open frame

priceRange.note: Official AlgoLaser store, Oct 2026: $459 machine with free air pump, $659 Basic kit (adds honeycomb, RR2 rotary roller and riser kit)

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cut: Basswood & plywood up to 12 mm (AlgoLaser claim, one pass)
cannot: Bare metal (no infrared module listed for the MK3)
Enclosed use without the optional enclosure

pros: AlgoLaser rates the module for 12 mm wood in a single pass
Air pump included even with the machine-only version
Fastest engraving of the MK3 range on the same 400 × 400 mm frame
cons: $150 more than the mid tier, and the 12 mm figure is unverified
More smoke and heat: an outdoor exhaust is a must, and the enclosure is a $299 extra
Larger module with no published spot size, so fine-detail performance is unknown
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W tier of the DIY Kit MK3. Compare it with the 15W: choose the 20W if you will cut wood every week, since the included air pump narrows the real price gap. For mostly engraving, the 15W is the better value.
proTips: Keep the air pump running for every cut and clean the lens window often: thick cuts foul it quickly. Treat 12 mm as a best case on soft wood; dense plywood and hardwood need slower speeds or extra passes. Vent outside or add the purifier, since cutting smoke builds up fast.

faq.question: Can the DIY Kit MK3 20W really cut 12 mm wood in one pass?
faq.answer: That is AlgoLaser's claim on its product images, and no independent test has confirmed it yet. Diode figures like this are usually measured on soft wood with air assist; plywood and hardwood take longer. In our benchmark, a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes about 5–8 min.

faq.question: Is the air pump really included?
faq.answer: Yes: on AlgoLaser's store in October 2026 the 20W machine is listed at $459 with a free air pump. The $659 Basic kit adds a honeycomb bed, the RR2 rotary roller and a riser kit.

faq.question: 20W MK3 or Alpha MK2 20W?
faq.answer: The MK3 20W is cheaper ($459 against $579 for the Alpha MK2 20W machine on AlgoLaser's store, October 2026) and adds a standalone touchscreen. The Alpha MK2 is a sturdier, more established frame with an optional infrared module for metal. Choose the MK3 for budget cutting, the Alpha for a longer-term workshop machine.

moduleSystem.headline: Three diode modules on the same MK3 frame
moduleSystem.description: The DIY Kit MK3 is sold with an 8W, 15W or 20W diode module on the same 400 × 400 mm frame and touchscreen. The power is chosen at purchase; modules fit the same head mount, one at a time.

editorialDepth.advantages: The 20W turns the MK3 into a budget cutting machine: a larger module, an air pump in the box and AlgoLaser's 12 mm one-pass rating, on a 400 × 400 mm frame with an offline touchscreen. For $459 it suits makers who cut signs and shapes every week.
editorialDepth.limitations: The cutting claim is unverified, the frame is open, and smoke management becomes a real cost at this power. Buyers who mostly engrave pay $150 for speed they will rarely use.

standoutFeatures.title: Air pump included
standoutFeatures.body: Unlike the 8W and 15W machine-only versions, the 20W ships with an air pump for cleaner cuts.
